item.text:
## 1B.6 Research Note: Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023

**Working judgment:** **Mostly no.** I found no reliable 2023 evidence that Putin resisted proliferation by an ally, proxy, client, or domestic faction when proliferation served short-term interests. The year’s clearest pattern is the opposite: he facilitated Russian tactical nuclear deployment in Belarus and publicly used it as coercive leverage.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 31.03.2023 г. № 229`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 31 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia’s updated foreign-policy concept declares support for strategic stability, nonproliferation, arms control, and reductions in nuclear risk. This is the main pro-restraint evidence, but it is generic doctrine and does not show Putin resisting ally or client proliferation in a concrete 2023 case.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.6`, `1B.4`, `1B.1`

- **Title:** `Russia signs deal to deploy tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, says they stay under its control`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 25 May 2023  
  **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/](https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia formalized deployment of tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus and said Moscow would retain control over them. This is strong evidence **against** 1B.6 because it shows Putin accepting, not resisting, proliferation-like forward deployment to a close ally when it served coercive and political interests.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.6`, `1B.5`, `1B.3`, `1B.1`

- **Title:** `Putin says Russia positions nuclear bombs in Belarus as warning to West`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 16 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-positions-nuclear-bombs-in-belarus-as-warning-to-west-3107500](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-positions-nuclear-bombs-in-belarus-as-warning-to-west-3107500)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin said tactical nuclear warheads had been delivered to Belarus as a warning to the West and a way to prevent strategic defeat. That is further evidence against 1B.6: nuclear capability was used to support coercive geopolitical aims, not restrained to prevent ally-enabled proliferation.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.6`, `1B.5`, `1B.2`, `1B.1`

- **Title:** `Putin publicly framed the tactical-nuclear drills in Belarus as training rather than actual use`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 16 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/74002)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin described the Belarus drills as exercises, not preparation for immediate use. This is the closest restraint-adjacent evidence I found, but it still sits inside a broader posture of Belarus nuclear deployment and does not show resistance to proliferation by an ally.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.6`, `1B.2`, `1B.3`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2023 evidence that Putin blocked or discouraged nuclear proliferation by Belarus or any other ally/client/proxy when doing so would have been politically useful. The available record points the other way: he accepted and publicized a forward nuclear deployment in Belarus. If a later reviewer wants a stricter standard, the safest reading is that **positive evidence is absent** rather than merely weak.

### Bottom line

**Mostly no.** The 2023 evidence does not show Putin resisting proliferation by allies or clients; it shows him tolerating and leveraging Belarus-based nuclear deployment for coercive purposes.
